title: The Wandering Star and Fleeting Wind
description: The Wandering Star and Fleeting Wind in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 326 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Inconstancy Lamented”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The wan-dering star and fleet-ing wind Are em-blems of the fick-le mind; The morn-ing cloud and ear-ly dew Bring our in-con-stan-cy to view.

lines: The wandering star and fleeting wind
Are emblems of the fickle mind;
The morning cloud and early dew
But cloud and wind and dew and star,
Nor can there aught in nature be
So changeable and frail as we.
Our outward walk and inward frame
Are scarcely through an hour the same:
We vow, and straight our vows forget,
And then those very vows repeat.
With contrite hearts, Lord, we confess
When shall these hearts more stable be,
Fixed by thy grace alone on thee?

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
